title: Efficacy and Safety of Adalimumab for the Treatment of Ocular Inflammation
off: Efficacy and Safety of Adalimumab in Pediatric Non-Infectious Uveitis: A Multicenter Ambispective Single-Arm Clinical Trial
summary: This study aims to evaluate the clinical efficacy and safety of adalimumab in pediatric non-infectious uveitis and to generate domestic real-world evidence (RWE), thereby establishing a clinical foundation for label expansion and reimbursement coverage.
desc: Background: Although anti-TNFα agents play a crucial role globally in managing refractory non-infectious uveitis, adalimumab was removed from the approved indication for pediatric uveitis in South Korea several years ago-unlike adult uveitis-making domestic prescription exceptionally difficult. Meanwhile, indications for pediatric idiopathic arthritis and pediatric Crohn's disease remain approved domestically, highlighting an urgent need to establish objective evidence to resolve this regulatory discrepancy. Furthermore, as a substantial number of pediatric patients in Korea are already receiving off-label, non-reimbursed adalimumab treatment, their real-world data serve both as evidence of efficacy and safety and as direct proof of this institutional imbalance.
elig:
Inclusion Criteria:

* For the Prospective New-User Cohort, verification of Inclusion Criteria 1 through 6 is required.
* For the Retrospective (Switch) Cohort, verification of Inclusion Criteria 1 through 7 is required.

  1. Pediatric patients aged 2 years and \< 18 years.
  2. Diagnosed with non-infectious anterior uveitis, intermediate uveitis, posterior uveitis, or panuveitis.
  3. Active intraocular inflammation demonstrated by anterior chamber (AC) cell grade ≥ 1+ (defined as 6 cells per 1 mm\\times 1 mm field) according to the SUN (Standardization of Uveitis Nomenclature) criteria, or active posterior segment lesions persistently observed on at least two consecutive assessments despite 12 weeks of treatment with methotrexate and corticosteroids (systemic or topical) prior to screening (SUN grade maintained on 2 occasions, adapted from the SYCAMORE trial definition of active disease).
  4. Inadequate response to corticosteroid therapy or other immunosuppressive agents (e.g., methotrexate \[MTX\]), or inability to continue treatment due to unacceptable toxicity/intolerance.
  5. Written informed consent obtained from the subject's legal representative (parent or legal guardian) and written pediatric assent obtained according to applicable age-specific regulatory and institutional guidelines.

     \[Prospective De Novo Cohort\]
  6. Patients initiating adalimumab for the first time (adalimumab-naïve).

\[Retrospective / Prospective Cohort\] 6. Patients currently on maintenance therapy with adalimumab (including extended dosing intervals, such as every other week \[Q2W\] or every 3-4 weeks) who require at least 1 additional year of treatment.

7\. Patients who agree to switch to the investigational product and adhere to a standard every-other-week (Q2W / once every 2 weeks) administration schedule at the time of study enrollment.

Exclusion Criteria:

* For the Prospective New-User Cohort, verification of Exclusion Criteria 1 through 22 is required.
* For the Retrospective (Switch) Cohort, verification of Exclusion Criteria 1 through 24 is required.

  1. Patients with uveitis associated with juvenile idiopathic arthritis (JIA) or pediatric Crohn's disease indicated for adalimumab
  2. Individuals with infectious uveitis or non-immunological intraocular inflammation resulting from trauma, surgery, etc., within 30 days prior to screening
  3. Individuals with active tuberculosis, untreated latent tuberculosis, sepsis, opportunistic infections, or other severe active infections, or those at high risk for such infections
  4. Individuals with a history of hypersensitivity to adalimumab or any of its excipients
  5. Individuals instilling topical glucocorticoids more than 6 times per eye per day, or currently receiving oral prednisone (or its equivalent) at a dose exceeding 0.2 mg/kg/day (adapted from the SYCAMORE criteria)
  6. Individuals with active malignancy, lymphoproliferative disorders, demyelinating disease (e.g., multiple sclerosis, Guillain-Barré syndrome), or a history of other progressive or degenerative neurological disorders
  7. Patients who have received TNF inhibitors other than the investigational product
  8. Patients with New York Heart Association (NYHA) Class III/IV cardiac disease
  9. Individuals with uncontrolled viral infections, including active hepatitis B or hepatitis C
  10. Individuals who have received a live vaccine (including live-attenuated vaccines) within 30 days prior to screening, or who are scheduled to receive one during the study period
  11. Individuals who are pregnant or breastfeeding, or women of childbearing potential (WOCBP) who do not agree to use highly effective contraception\*

      \*A highly effective method of contraception is defined as one that results in a low failure rate of less than 1% per year when used consistently and correctly, and includes: combined (estrogen- and progestogen-containing) hormonal contraception associated with inhibition of ovulation (oral, intravaginal, transdermal); progestogen-only hormonal contraception associated with inhibition of ovulation (oral, injectable, implantable); intrauterine device (IUD); intrauterine hormone-releasing system (IUS); bilateral tubal occlusion; vasectomized partner; and sexual abstinence.
  12. Individuals who have received other biologic agents within 5 half-lives prior to screening
  13. Individuals with a family member who has active tuberculosis, or who have a history of close contact with an individual with active tuberculosis
  14. Individuals with a major infection requiring antibiotic therapy within 30 days prior to screening
  15. Individuals with diabetes mellitus deemed uncontrolled by the investigator, or persistently uncontrolled severe hypertension (\> 95th percentile for height and age)
  16. Individuals with a history of malignancy, or a history of solid organ, bone marrow, or corneal transplantation
  17. Individuals with a history of ocular surgery (e.g., cataract surgery) within 3 months prior to screening
  18. Individuals who have received intraocular or periocular corticosteroid injections within 30 days prior to screening
  19. Individuals with a history of ocular herpes simplex or herpes zoster infection
  20. Individuals with laboratory values evaluated during screening that meet any of the following criteria:

      A. Hemoglobin \< 8.0 g/dL B. WBC \< 4.0 × 10³/µL C. ANC \< 1.0 × 10³/µL D. Platelet count \< 100 × 10³/µL E. AST or ALT \> 2 × ULN
  21. Individuals weighing less than 15 kg
  22. Individuals otherwise deemed unsuitable for study participation in the judgment of the investigator

      \[Retrospective / Prospective Cohort-Specific Criteria\]
  23. Inability to confirm disease activity (e.g., SUN grading) at the initial start of adalimumab treatment and subsequent treatment response via medical record review.
  24. Patients whose adalimumab dosage has been tapered to near-discontinuation (i.e., dosing intervals substantially exceeding once every 4 weeks) or for whom the treating physician deems the standard maintenance regimen (once every 2 weeks) clinically inappropriate.

arms.d:
Prospective Cohort: Adalimumab-naïve patients will receive the investigational product (an adalimumab biosimilar) for 12 months (approximately 52 weeks) after enrollment.

Retrospective (Switch) Cohort: Adalimumab-experienced patients who require at least 1 additional year of treatment will switch to the investigational product at enrollment.

primary.m: Treatment Failure Rate in the Prospective Treatment-Naïve Cohort
primary.tf: Up to 12 months after adalimumab initiation

primary.m: Change from Baseline in Medically Important Infections (MIIS) in the Prospective Treatment-Naïve Cohort
primary.tf: Baseline and 12 months after adalimumab initiation

Adalimumab plus Methotrexate for Uveitis in Juvenile Idiopathic Arthritis. N Engl J Med. 2017 Apr 27;376(17):1637-1646. doi: 10.1056/NEJMoa1614160.

x.titre: Adalimumab biosimilaire dans l'uvéite non infectieuse de l'enfant en Corée du Sud (PANDA-U)
x.question: L'adalimumab est-il efficace et sûr chez l'enfant atteint d'uvéite non infectieuse, pour produire des données en vie réelle en Corée du Sud ?
x.contexte:
L'uvéite non infectieuse de l'enfant (antérieure, intermédiaire, postérieure ou panuvéite) peut être chronique et menacer la vision. Après échec des corticoïdes et du méthotrexate, les anti-TNF, dont l'adalimumab, jouent un rôle central dans les formes réfractaires. L'essai SYCAMORE a servi de référence pour définir l'activité de la maladie.

En Corée du Sud, l'indication pédiatrique de l'adalimumab dans l'uvéite a été retirée il y a plusieurs années, à la différence de l'adulte. Les indications dans l'arthrite juvénile idiopathique et la maladie de Crohn pédiatrique restent approuvées. De nombreux enfants reçoivent donc de l'adalimumab hors AMM et sans remboursement, ce que les promoteurs veulent documenter.

PANDA-U est une étude monocentrique du Samsung Medical Center, en ouvert, à un seul groupe, d'environ 40 enfants de 2 à 18 ans. Une cohorte prospective de patients naïfs d'adalimumab reçoit un biosimilaire pendant 12 mois. Une cohorte de relais comprend des patients déjà traités qui passent au produit étudié. L'objectif est de constituer des données de vie réelle pour appuyer une extension d'indication et le remboursement.
x.interet: L'étude pourrait servir d'appui à un rétablissement de l'indication pédiatrique et au remboursement de l'adalimumab dans l'uvéite en Corée du Sud. Elle apporte aussi des données sur un biosimilaire chez l'enfant.
x.profil: Des enfants de 2 à 17 ans atteints d'uvéite non infectieuse antérieure, intermédiaire, postérieure ou panuvéite, en échec des traitements usuels.
inclusion: Âge de 2 ans à moins de 18 ans
Uvéite non infectieuse (antérieure, intermédiaire, postérieure ou panuvéite)
Inflammation active (cellules en chambre antérieure ≥ 1+ selon SUN, ou lésions postérieures persistantes malgré 12 semaines de méthotrexate et corticoïdes)
Réponse insuffisante ou intolérance aux corticoïdes ou aux immunosuppresseurs
Consentement des parents et assentiment de l'enfant
Cohorte prospective : adalimumab jamais utilisé ; cohorte de relais : adalimumab en cours, avec au moins 1 an de traitement à poursuivre, et schéma toutes les 2 semaines
exclusion: Uvéite associée à une arthrite juvénile idiopathique ou à une maladie de Crohn pédiatrique
Uvéite infectieuse ou inflammation d'origine non immunologique (traumatisme, chirurgie) dans les 30 jours
Tuberculose active ou latente non traitée, sepsis, infection opportuniste ou infection sévère active
Hypersensibilité à l'adalimumab ou à ses excipients
Corticoïdes topiques > 6 instillations par jour et par œil
Autres critères d'exclusion (22 à 24) non détaillés dans l'extrait du registre

bras.traitement: Biosimilaire de l'adalimumab (seringue préremplie ou stylo), toutes les 2 semaines ; cohorte prospective pendant 12 mois, cohorte de relais pour au moins 1 an

x.duree: 12 mois (environ 52 semaines) pour la cohorte prospective
x.critere: Taux d'échec thérapeutique et variation des infections médicalement importantes (MIIS) dans la cohorte prospective de patients naïfs, jusqu'à 12 mois.
